S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by disturbances in thought, perception, behavior, and affect, typically including delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking/behavior, and negative symptoms such as diminished motivation and emotional expression. Onset most commonly occurs in late adolescence or early adulthood, but late-onset cases can occur, especially in women and in the context of significant psychosocial or medical stressors. The course is usually protracted, with episodes of exacerbation and partial remission, and functional decline in work, self-care, and social relationships is common if untreated. It is distinguished from mood disorders with psychotic features by the presence of persistent psychotic symptoms outside of mood episodes, and from brief psychotic or schizophreniform disorders by its duration and degree of functional impairment.

patient.personality: A meticulous, rule‑driven and solitary man, he channels his chronic worry into strict routines, careful planning, and quiet, detail‑oriented hobbies like woodworking and birdwatching.
patient.stressor: About a year and a half ago, Salah’s plant announced a major restructuring, with automation upgrades that threatened many positions and made his long‑pursued shift‑supervisor role suddenly uncertain. Already a chronic worrier who coped through control and precision, he responded by doubling down on procedures, staying late to check machines, and obsessively reviewing manuals and budgets at home, gradually becoming more withdrawn from coworkers and his usual weekend activities. Over the following months, coworkers noticed him losing track of tasks, standing motionless on the line, and abandoning projects in his workshop as his usual drive and engagement with work and hobbies eroded, leading to repeated safety write‑ups and forced medical leave. When he began missing shifts, neglecting basic home upkeep, and sitting for long periods staring into his garden instead of fishing or volunteering, his sister and plant HR jointly pushed him to see a psychiatrist because he seemed to have “shut down” and could no longer reliably function at work or manage daily responsibilities.
patient.chief_complaint: “I don’t feel like doing anything anymore, and I’ve kind of stopped talking to people.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Ever since the company started talking about the robots and the restructuring, I’ve become convinced that management and some of the guys on the floor are slipping my name into reports and even hiding cameras in the machine housings to watch me at home, and no matter what anyone says I can’t shake the feeling they’re trying to build a case to get rid of me or worse.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: Most days now, especially when I’m alone in the house or out by the garden, I hear this low man’s voice right behind me commenting on what I’m doing—telling me I’m doing it wrong at the machines, that I’ve ruined everything—and sometimes I see shadows move in the hallway or out by the shed even though I know nobody’s there.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: At work and even in my workshop at home, I’ll catch myself just freezing in place, staring at a bolt or a board for ten, fifteen minutes, or pacing back and forth and muttering through the steps under my breath, and when people speak to me I either don’t answer or I repeat what they just said without meaning to, like my body’s stuck in some wrong gear.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: These days I mostly sit in my chair looking out at the yard, ignoring calls from my sister and the guys from the fishing club, letting the dishes and laundry pile up, and even when I try to start a birdhouse or pick up the phone, it’s like there’s no energy or feeling in me to follow through or even care what happens.
